subject: FinBank evals: post-demo recap, recommended models & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Emily Nguyen <emily.nguyen@finbank.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, David Kim <david@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: FinBank evals: post-demo recap, recommended models & next steps

Hi Emily —

Thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get a focused, customer-specific eval running on Redwood: 

Recap (from today)
- Goal: surface accurate, auditable answers from financial documents and internal policy texts for customer support routing and policy compliance automation.
- Priority metrics: factual accuracy, hallucination rate, and semantic match to gold responses.
- Data: FinBank will provide an anonymized sample set (~3-5k rows) covering common question types and edge cases (PII redacted).

Recommended evaluation plan (high level)
1) Models to benchmark (we'll run all on Redwood and provide single report):
   - redwood-instruct-3b (fast, low-cost baseline)
   - redwood-rl-7b (balanced quality/latency)
   - llama-13b-q4_0 (open-model high-quality variant we host)
2) Dataset format: JSONL, one record per line. Required fields: id, prompt, expected_response, category, metadata (optional). Example stub attached.
3) Prompt sets: we suggest separate prompt templates for: extraction, multi-turn clarification, and policy interpretation. See attached finbank_eval_prompts_v1.txt.
4) Scoring criteria:
   - Exact / token overlap (for short extracted spans)
   - Semantic similarity: embedding cosine (we use a 0-1 scale; recommend pass threshold >= 0.85)
   - Regression checks: compare each model run to your current baseline; we flag >2% drop in accuracy or >5% increase in hallucination rate as a regression

Security & deployment note
- We can run the evals on Redwood Hosted for speed, or on a Dedicated/Private instance if you need VPC isolation. We recommend Dedicated for production-quality evals with your full dataset.

Next steps (proposed)
1) You share an anonymized sample JSONL (3–5k rows) — see sample attached.
2) We provision an eval workspace and run the three model variants across the dataset (turnaround: 2–3 business days after provisioning).
3) We deliver a scored report (metrics, per-category fail cases, representative prompts) and then schedule a 30-min results sync.

Attachments included: finbank_sample_dataset.jsonl (sample, 200 rows), finbank_eval_prompts_v1.txt

Questions for you:
- Are there any additional automatic metrics your security/compliance team requires (e.g., PII detection pass/fail)?
- Do you want the eval executed in your VPC/Dedicated environment or is Hosted OK for this run?

Happy to adjust the plan — if this looks good I’ll loop in engineering and start the provisioning.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: finbank_sample_dataset.jsonl 
Attachment: finbank_eval_prompts_v1.txt]

From: Emily Nguyen <emily.nguyen@finbank.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Rajiv Menon <rajiv.menon@finbank.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FinBank evals: post-demo recap, recommended models & next steps

Thanks, Marissa — really helpful summary. A couple of quick follow-ups from our side: 

1) Security/PII: we'll only share an anonymized sample, but Rajiv (cc'd) will need details on where the data will be stored and for how long. If you can provide SOC2 evidence and a short note about retention and KMS/HSM usage, that will speed approvals.

2) Eval environment: for the initial benchmark we prefer Dedicated (VPC) so we can mirror production routing and network controls. Is that something you can provision for a short soak (3–5 days)?

3) Scoring thresholds: the suggested embedding threshold (0.85) sounds reasonable. For hallucination detection, do you have an automated detector you run or is that manual review?

Happy to sync. Can we schedule a 30-min call after you provision and complete runs?

Thanks,
Emily
Product Lead, Conversational AI
FinBank

Hi Emily / Rajiv —

Great questions. Quick answers and what we can do immediately: 

Security & data handling- We will only accept the anonymized JSONL sample (no raw PII).
- Storage: for Dedicated runs we can provision a VPC-backed instance that stores artifacts in your VPC or in an encrypted S3 bucket controlled by your KMS. We support customer-managed KMS/HSM and audit logs.
- Evidence: attaching our Redwood security package (SOC2 summary + network & KMS notes). If Rajiv wants any additional artifacts we can arrange a security review.

Hallucination detection- We run a hybrid approach: automatic heuristics (extraction-confidence thresholds, pattern-based checks) plus sampling for manual review on low-confidence cases. We'll include per-example confidence scores in the report so your team can triage.

Dedicated provisioning- We can provision a short-lived Dedicated eval slice (3–5 days). Neha (cc'd) will own provisioning and will confirm the instance size we recommend based on dataset size.

Next steps
1) Rajiv: can you confirm whether you want the eval artifacts stored in your VPC (preferred) or in an encrypted Redwood bucket?
2) Emily: please share the anonymized JSONL sample (or a shared Drive link).
3) Neha: will you confirm provisioning plan and timeline?

I’ve attached our security package and the prompt set again.

Thanks,
Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
